newsitem.title: USA: Boeing says contract worth $5.6 billion.
newsitem.headline: Boeing says contract worth $5.6 billion.

text.p: A contract to build an airborne laser system to shoot down ballistic missiles could be worth $5.6 billion over the next 12 years, a Boeing Co executive said Tuesday.
The Pentagon announced earlier that a team led by Boeing won a $1.1 billion contract to develop a prototype airplane that would be demonstrated in 2002.

If successful the Air Force would award a second contract in July 2004 worth an estimated $4.5 billion to develop a fully operational fleet of seven airplanes including the prototype, Boeing Vice President Dick Hardy said.

Hardy, general manager of Boeing's military airplane division, told reporters in a telephone news conference, that the laser-equipped airplanes would join the Air Force fleet by a target date of June 2006 and all seven would be operational by June 2008.

While the initial systems will be mounted in modified Boeing 747 jumbo jets, Hardy said that ultimately the laser equipment is likely to get smaller and lighter and will be able to be placed in smaller airframes.
"The system is going to get better," Hardy said. "The performance is going to go up, the weight is going to go down and the volume is going to go down."
He said the contract would result in only a few more jobs at Boeing in the short term and "hundreds" in the long term.
Lockheed Martin Corp and TRW Inc also were part of the Boeing team.
